newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert gets FDA OK for Lipitor cholesterol drug.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert gets FDA OK for Lipitor cholesterol drug.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co. said Wednesday the Food and Drug Administration cleared Lipitor, which has produced dramatic results in the treatment of high cholesterol, for sale in the United States.
The company said Lipitor is the only drug in its class specifically indicated for lowering both elevated LDL-cholesterol and triglycerides in patients with high cholesterol.
It said that while 52 million American adults need treatment for high cholesterol, less than one-third of those who could benefit from medication are now taking it.

In placebo-controlled, dose-response studies in patients with high cholesterol, Lipitor significantly reduced elevated LDL-cholesterol -- the so-called "bad cholesterol" -- by 40 to 60 percent across the dose range of 10 mg to 80 mg administered once daily, the company said.
In addition, Lipitor lowered triglycerides -- fatty substances in the blood that are believed to contribute to coronary heart disease -- by 20 to 40 percent.
Lipitor tablets are an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, or "statin."

Warner-Lambert said that in clinical trials, Lipitor was superior to other statins, including Merck & Co.'s Zocor and Mevacor and Bristol-Myers Squibb's Pravachol at reducing elevated total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol and triglycerides.

"The ability of Lipitor to dramatically reduce both elevated LDL-cholesterol and triglycerides enables the medical community to enter a new era of cholesterol management," said Melvin Goodes, chairman and chief executive officer of Warner-Lambert.
The starting dose of Lipitor is 10 mg taken as a single daily dose at any time during the day, with or without food, the company said.

"The National Cholesterol Education Programme has set guidelines for reducing cholesterol, yet many of those people receiving treatment are not reaching treatment goals," said Donald Hunninghake, director of the Heart Disease Prevention Clinic at the University of Minnesota Hospital in Minneapolis, Minn.

"There is a need for more aggressive management of high cholesterol, he said. "The introduction of Lipitor provides a new option in lipid management because of its ability to lower both elevated LDL-cholesterol and triglycerides at the starting dose, allowing physicians to effectively and conveniently treat a large group of patients."
Warner-Lambert's Parke-Davis division developed Lipitor and recently entered into an agreement with Pfizer Inc. under which both companies will market the drug in the United States and abroad.
Recently, Lipitor was approved for sale in Germany and Britain.
Warner-Lambert's stock gained $2.125 to $76.375 and Pfizer added $1.75 to $82.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
